# ast perf baseline — body-free counting and single-pass splice apply.
#
# WALL-CLOCK IS NOT A GATED AXIS OF THIS PLAN. Every gate in the plan asserts
# allocations or retained bytes — properties of the code, not of the machine it
# ran on. The ns/op figures below are recorded as OBSERVATIONS only. The
# ticket's before-figure carried a 9.2s reading while the count walk itself
# re-derives at ~805ms; that gap is GC pressure from holding an ~808MB live set
# plus response marshaling, not the walk. Removing that live set is plausibly
# why a wall-clock improvement would appear, but this plan does not claim it and
# does not gate on it. Never read an ns/op line here as a criterion that was met.
#
# The two allocs/op lines are the RUN-PROOF: a `go test -bench` invocation exits
# 0 when its selector matches nothing and prints no `--- PASS:` line, so the
# benchmarks' existence is gated structurally (comment-stripped perf_bench_test.go)
# and the proof they actually ran is that each contributed an allocs/op figure
# here — a benchmark that never ran produces none.
#
# MACHINE STATE: Apple M4 Max (goarch arm64, 16 logical CPUs), darwin. Captured
# on branch wt-perf. The
# count corpus is a non-git temp dir, so its walk logs the expected
# "git ls-files failed, falling back to filesystem walk" per the nongit
# discovery path — not an error.

BEFORE

HEAD: faa646c56754d650f38c5bb39fd9227a0bc0788d

# Splice shape measured: right-to-left whole-buffer rebuild (the shape Phase 1
# extracted verbatim from applyEditsToSource into spliceEdits — seed
# `out := append([]byte{}, src...)` plus a per-edit
# `append(append(append([]byte{}, out[:Start]...), repl...), out[End:]...)`
# rebuild). 400 disjoint DESC-sorted edits over a ~4,000-line buffer. Its ~800
# allocs/op is a KNOWN-POSITIVE control for Phase 2, whose forward-pass rewrite
# drives allocations to a small constant independent of edit count (<20 at 400).
BenchmarkSpliceEdits_ManyEdits-16    	 207	  5918850 ns/op	91302948 B/op	   798 allocs/op

# Count-walk shape measured: ast.Match — the full walk that RETAINS every
# RawMatch across the whole scope. 40 fixed Go files, ~200 matches each,
# placeholder-rooted `$_`. The ~289k allocs/op reflects that walk-wide
# retention; it is what Phase 3's body-free count path removes.
BenchmarkCountWalk_PlaceholderRoot-16	  48	 27840985 ns/op	80661874 B/op	289050 allocs/op

# RETENTION CLAIM the AFTER block is allowed to make, stated precisely: after
# Phase 3, peak retention on the count path is O(files) PLUS one largest-file
# transient times NumCPU — NOT a bare "O(files)". The per-file []RawMatch a
# worker builds still exists while that file is being tallied; what the change
# removes is the walk-wide accumulation of every file's matches. BEFORE, the
# count path retains O(matches): every RawMatch across the whole scope is held
# until the response is built.

AFTER

HEAD: 1a92e43228860496bf524f7918d5573bd0af6db5

# Measured at the Phase 3 HEAD on the same machine (Apple M4 Max, arm64, 16
# logical CPUs, darwin), branch wt-perf, clean tree. Same wall-clock caveat as
# the BEFORE block: ns/op is an observation, never a gated axis.

# Splice shape measured: single forward pass with exact pre-size (Phase 2). Same
# 400 disjoint DESC-sorted edits over the ~4,000-line buffer. Allocations
# collapsed from ~798 to 1 — a small CONSTANT independent of edit count, which
# is the gated property (TestSpliceEdits_AllocationsAreIndependentOfEditCount:
# forward <20, right-to-left reference control >400). ns/op fell ~490x as a
# by-product, recorded as observation only.
BenchmarkSpliceEdits_ManyEdits-16    	 97627	    12022 ns/op	  147456 B/op	     1 allocs/op

# Count-walk shape measured: ast.Count — the body-free walk (Phase 3). Same 40
# fixed Go files, ~200 matches each, placeholder-rooted `$_`.
# allocs/op AND ns/op are essentially UNCHANGED from BEFORE, and that is
# CORRECT, not a null result: the count path still BUILDS every per-file
# RawMatch (the walk is untouched — the scope question ruled count stops
# RETAINING, not building, since the 805ms/874k-match walk showed the 808MB was
# retention). The win is PEAK RETENTION, which allocs/op cannot show: it drops
# from O(matches) to O(files) PLUS one largest-file []RawMatch transient times
# NumCPU — the per-file slice a worker holds only while tallying that file. That
# property is proven by TestCount_RetainsNoMatchBodies (Count flat across a 10x
# match jump at fixed file count; the Match arm scales >5x as the known-positive
# control). B/op fell ~10% because the walk-wide results-slice append growth is
# gone.
BenchmarkCountWalk_PlaceholderRoot-16	  40	 27071501 ns/op	72512273 B/op	289168 allocs/op

# ============================================================================
# alloc-storm — placeholder-rooted match/count/replace allocation fixes.
#
# Four fixes to the placeholder-rooted (rootQuery==nil → collectViaWalk) path,
# each gated by an AllocsPerRun assertion elsewhere; these benchmark lines are
# the RUN-PROOF record, never a gate (same convention as the blocks above: a
# `go test -bench` selector that matches nothing still exits 0). BenchmarkMatchWalk_
# PlaceholderRoot is the shared record for fix #1 (skip dead $match/nodes on the
# where==nil path) and fix #3 (drop the per-match fresh newCaptures/nodes alloc).
# Same machine/caveat as above: ns/op is an observation, allocs/op is the gated
# property mirrored by the AllocsBounded tests.
#
# MACHINE STATE: Apple M4 Max (goarch arm64, 16 logical CPUs), darwin. Captured
# on branch wt-allocstorm. The count/match corpus is benchCountCorpus — a non-git
# temp dir, so its walk logs the expected "git ls-files failed, falling back to
# filesystem walk" per the nongit discovery path — not an error.

BEFORE

HEAD: 32d57a72055b27dad8a0e0f670cb84d0c0301efd

# Match-walk shape measured: ast.Match over benchCountCorpus (40 fixed Go files,
# ~200 matches each), placeholder-rooted `$_`, where==nil. Every named node
# matches, so tryMatch runs matchTreeWithNodes for each — the $match nodeToCapture
# Content copy + findNodeBySpan nodes loop (dead when where==nil, fix #1) plus a
# fresh newCaptures/nodes map per successful match (fix #3). That is the ~289k
# allocs/op the two fixes remove.
BenchmarkMatchWalk_PlaceholderRoot-16	  39	 29240438 ns/op	80658595 B/op	289040 allocs/op

AFTER

HEAD: wt-allocstorm (fix #1 + fix #3 applied)

# Same machine (Apple M4 Max, arm64, 16 logical CPUs, darwin), same corpus and
# `$_` where==nil pattern. Fix #1 (skip the dead $match/nodes work on where==nil)
# and fix #3 (drop the per-match fresh newCaptures/nodes alloc) together take the
# placeholder-root Match path 289040 -> 98276 allocs/op (66%), 80.6MB -> 46.4MB
# B/op. Attribution between the two is locked by the AllocsBounded gates: fix #1
# alone lands ~215071 (TestMatch_WhereNil_AllocsBounded ceiling 230000), fix #3
# takes it the rest of the way (TestMatch_PlaceholderRoot_AllocsBounded ceiling
# 130000). ns/op is an observation only, never a gated axis.
BenchmarkMatchWalk_PlaceholderRoot-16	  56	 21030302 ns/op	46446757 B/op	 98276 allocs/op

# Count-walk shape measured: ast.Count over the SAME corpus, placeholder-rooted
# `$_`. The count light-match path (fix #2) binds a body-free {span, kind} per
# match instead of a RawMatch, so it neither builds a per-match Captures map nor
# copies node source. Count drops 289167 -> 24466 allocs/op (92%), 80.6MB ->
# 8.7MB B/op — the largest fix. Gated TIGHT by TestCount_LightMatch_AllocsBounded
# (ceiling 30000, just above the post-fix value); correctness held by the
# Match-oracle parity test TestCount_LightMatchParity.
BenchmarkCountWalk_PlaceholderRoot-16	  72	 15822735 ns/op	 8735696 B/op	 24466 allocs/op

# ============================================================================
# JSX layout whitespace — concrete-rooted JSX match walk.
#
# PRE-FIX BASELINE, taken BEFORE the token-comparison change, and taken then
# because measuring afterwards would bake the trim's own cost into the ceiling
# meant to detect it.
#
# WHICH ARM IT BOUNDS, and why that is NOT the arm it was recorded from. This row
# was measured from BenchmarkMatchWalk_JSXConcreteRoot, whose pattern matches the
# corpus once the defect is fixed. The GATED arm is BenchmarkMatchWalk_JSXNoMatch,
# whose pattern matches nothing in either state. The distinction is the whole
# reason that second benchmark exists: pre-fix this corpus produced ZERO matches
# (nothing matching WAS the defect), so gating the matching arm against this row
# would compare thousands of materialised matches against none and go red exactly
# because the fix worked — measured 89459 against a 35137 ceiling. A before/after
# allocation ceiling is only valid when both runs do the same work, and a fix
# whose purpose is to make an empty result set non-empty changes the work. The
# no-match arm produces zero matches on both sides, so the two differ only by the
# trim: measured 32480 against this row's 29281, about +11%, which is the extra
# per-candidate descent the trim unlocks rather than the trim allocating.
# BenchmarkMatchWalk_JSXConcreteRoot remains INFORMATIONAL and is never a gate.
#
# EXACTLY ONE LINE IN THIS FILE MAY CARRY THE BASELINE LABEL — the token on the
# data row below, spelled here only there because the gate counts raw
# occurrences and prose quoting it would inflate the count. This file's
# convention is to APPEND readings — three benchmarks above appear two or three
# times each for that reason — so the ceiling gate identifies its baseline by a
# unique token rather than by position, and asserts exactly one such line exists.
# A second labelled row fails that gate loudly, by design: an extraction that
# silently took the newest row would compare the post-fix number against itself
# and pass an arbitrarily large regression. A post-fix reading recorded for the
# record must carry a DIFFERENT label.
#
# Corpus: benchJSXCorpus — 40 synthetic .tsx files, each with 40 multi-line JSX
# children under one parent element. Pattern `<CodeBlock code={$C} />`
# (concrete-rooted, so it reaches the childless-token comparison; the
# placeholder-rooted benchmarks above return at the node-wildcard arm and cannot).
#
# MACHINE STATE: Apple M4 Max (goarch arm64, 16 logical CPUs), darwin, branch
# main, clean tree. The corpus is a non-git temp dir, so its walk logs the
# expected "git ls-files failed, falling back to filesystem walk" per the nongit
# discovery path — not an error. ns/op is an observation only, never a gated
# axis; allocs/op is the gated property.

BEFORE
